title: $f^!$ with finite coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an arbitrary field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting; def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $A$ be any finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, given the discrete topology, and write $\underline A$ for its condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For each such scheme $T$, identify the pulled-back ring object $p_T^*\underline A$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] with the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. Use the section-action equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to identify internal $p_T^*\underline A$-module objects with ordinary $A_T$-module sheaves, and its termwise derived equivalence to identify their derived categories. Under this exact, tensor-compatible equivalence, write $\Dctf(T,A)$ for the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory: the module-object definition is [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and its ordinary-module form is [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf; def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Let $\Loc(\Dctf(T,A))$ be the full triangulated closure under arbitrary small sums of [sk-def-localizing-closure], identified by that same equivalence. Let
$$f^!: \Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$$
be the right adjoint to $Rf_!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence], with both functors viewed in these identified categories. Then
$$f^!\bigl(\Dctf(Y,A)\bigr)\subseteq\Dctf(X,A).$$
Consequently this adjunction restricts to
$$Rf_!: \Dctf(X,A)\ \rightleftarrows\ \Dctf(Y,A):f^!.$$
For smooth $f$ of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], its restriction is étale locally on $X$ naturally isomorphic to $f^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Here choose $N=\ell^r\geq1$ annihilating $A$ and define the pro-étale twist $A_T(d)$ to be $\nu_T^*$ of the ordinary étale twist of [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], using the exact site-comparison pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]; $(-)(d)$ means derived tensor with this line. The canonical global isomorphism is constructed separately in the smooth-purity chapter.

proof.text: We first work on the ordinary small étale sites. Write $f^{\times}$ for the right adjoint to the ordinary étale $Rf_!$. Finite-type $k$-schemes are Noetherian, and are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. An open subscheme is again Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. In particular its intersection with any affine open of the target is quasi-compact, so every open immersion used here is quasi-compact and hence finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. For an open subscheme $U\subseteq T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], the fiber product $U\times_TU$ identifies with $U$ with both projections the identity; its diagonal is therefore an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion, so the open immersion is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Nagata gives a compactification for every separated finite-type morphism in question, including the closed immersions, affine-space projections, and open restrictions used below. Thus the ordinary étale adjoints exist on the entire ordinary derived categories, independently of any preservation assertion. Fix $N=\ell^r\geq1$ annihilating $A$; $N$ is invertible on all these schemes. For later use, Tor intervals on an étale site can be tested on geometric stalks: by exactness of stalks and the derived tensor/pullback comparison, $(K\otimes_A^L M)_{\bar x}\simeq K_{\bar x}\otimes_A^L M_{\bar x}$. Testing first with constant sheaves of arbitrary $A$-modules proves the necessary stalkwise bounds, and conservativity of the geometric stalks proves sufficiency for arbitrary module sheaves. Consequently exact inverse image along any scheme morphism preserves a Tor interval: at a source point the tensor is the tensor of the target stalk with the given source module stalk. These arguments include the zero ring and zero complex.

source.place: Opening reduction to closed immersions and smooth projections; ordinary étale adjoint and stalkwise tensor preliminaries. Stacks Tags 01T6, 07A4; Zheng Proposition 3.16(2).

proof.text: Consider a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between schemes of the stated setting and its complementary open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow T$. The complement is Noetherian and $j$ is quasi-compact, separated and finite type by step 1; $V,T$ are finite-type $k$-schemes. Choose a nonnegative integer $e\geq\operatorname{cd}(j)$ using clause (1) of [lem-kun-0f10] and [def-kun-cd]. This is relative cohomological dimension over an arbitrary field; it does not require finite cohomological dimension of $k$. Every $A$-module sheaf has torsion underlying abelian sheaf, since $\ell^r A=0$. The higher-direct-image forgetful comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] therefore gives $R^qj_*M=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ and every $q>e$. For a constructible $A$-sheaf $F$, apply [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] to $F[0]$ and $j$: $Rj_*F$ is bounded constructible, so each $R^qj_*F$ is constructible. Its coefficient hypothesis holds because $A$ is finite and annihilated by $\ell^r$, invertible in $k$. These are exactly the two hypotheses of [lem-exc-closed-amplitude], with $c=e$. It follows that the ordinary closed right adjoint sends a constructible cohomological interval $[r,s]$ to $[r,s+e+1]$. It agrees with $i^{\times}$: use the compactification $Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Z\xrightarrow{i}T$, for which compact supports are $Ri_*=i_*$, and compare the natural adjunction bijections. The closed immersion is finite and proper by the cited statements. Its exact direct image on abelian sheaves is exact on module sheaves as well, because exactness is detected after forgetting the action. Thus the support triangle in the next step uses this same $i^{\times}$. If $T$ or $V$ is empty the same argument applies, with zero direct image for empty $V$ and, if needed, $e=0$.

source.place: Closed-immersion support-triangle paragraph, using general-field ordinary direct-image finiteness (thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility) and Stacks Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd (1), in place of a separably-closed-field bound.

proof.text: For the closed case let $K$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, put $L=j^*K$ and $Q=Rj_*L$. Step 1 gives the same Tor interval for $L$, and step 2 gives a nonnegative uniform bound $e$ on all module higher direct images. The finite ring $A$ is Noetherian (every chain of ideals stabilizes), and every finite $A$-module $M$ is finitely presented: a finite free presentation has finite, hence finitely generated, kernel. The bounded constructible complex $L$ belongs to $D^-$. Thus [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant], with this $e$, gives the projection isomorphism for every finite constant module $M$. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sf-open-tor-bound-arbitrary-field], which gives $Q$ Tor amplitude $[a,b+e]$. Apply [lem-sf-closed-support-tor-bound] to the distinguished support triangle of step 2. Exactness of $i_*$ is established there, and $i^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The counit $i^*i_*G\to G$ is an isomorphism by [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful], applied to the underlying abelian sheaves: an $A$-linear map of module sheaves whose underlying map of abelian sheaves is invertible is invertible. Hence $i^\times K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b+e+1]$. Its bounded constructibility follows from step 2.

source.place: Closed-immersion paragraph: arbitrary-field open Tor bound, support triangle contributes +1.

proof.text: Let $p:P\to V$ be a separated smooth morphism of pure relative dimension $m$ between finite-type $k$-schemes. This includes the affine-space projections, whose separatedness is checked in step 7; compactifiability follows from step 1. The ordinary étale smooth tensor theorem provides a locally constant free rank-one sheaf $L$ and natural isomorphisms $p^{\times}K\simeq p^*K\otimes_A^L L[2m]$. Pullback is exact and preserves constructible sheaves. Tensor with $L$ is locally tensor with $A$, hence exact; on each constructible stratum it preserves the finite locally constant models, so the resulting sheaves are constructible. Therefore a cohomological interval $[r,s]$ changes to $[r-2m,s-2m]$. Step 1 gives Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $p^*K$. At every geometric stalk tensor with $L$ is tensor with a free rank-one module, so it preserves this interval; the shift then gives $[a-2m,b-2m]$. This proves the smooth case of preservation without using a theorem that already assumes preservation, and it proves the affine-space case needed for the chart argument.

source.place: Affine-space/smooth paragraph: the unoriented local line and tensor formula, rather than an assumed preservation datum. Zheng Proposition 3.16(2), smooth case.

proof.text:
Here is the chart identification, made before restricting exceptional functors. Let $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $s:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open immersions with $f(U)\subseteq V$, and let $fs=vpi$, with $i:U\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A^m_V$ closed and $p:P\to V$ the projection. For every $H\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the exact open-extension adjunction, compact-support composition for $fs=vpi$, and the ordinary étale adjunctions give natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(H,s^*f^{\times}K)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(s_!H,f^{\times}K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!s_!H,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rp_!i_*H,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!i_*H,v^*K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,i^{\times}p^{\times}v^*K).
\end{aligned}$$
Every input to the compact-support composition comparison is bounded below: $s_!$, $v_!$, and $i_*$ are exact, and the compact-support candidates $Rr_*j_!$ send $D^+$ to $D^+$. This last assertion follows by choosing a bounded-below injective resolution after the exact extension by zero. The comparison theorem is therefore used only in its stated range. Steps 2–4 put $B=i^{\times}p^{\times}v^*K$ in $D^+$ for bounded constructible finite-Tor $K$. Evaluate the inverse of the displayed bijection at $H=B$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$ to obtain $\alpha:B\to s^*f^{\times}K$. Naturality in bounded-below $H$ says that $\operatorname{Hom}(H,\alpha)$ is bijective, including for every shift of $H$. Step 6 shows this suffices even if $s^*f^{\times}K$ is not yet known bounded below. Consequently $s^*f^{\times}K\simeq i^{\times}p^{\times}v^*K$.

source.place: Final paragraph, composition and open locality: Hom calculations spelling out the restriction to each chart.

proof.text:
The bounded-below test used in step 5 has a direct proof. If $\alpha:B\to G$ induces bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(H[n],B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H[n],G)$ for all bounded-below $H$ and integers $n$, its cone $C$ has $\operatorname{Hom}(H[n],C)=0$. Represent $C$ by a cochain complex $E^\bullet$. Its brutal lower tails $E_{\geq -r}^\bullet$, with zero terms below $-r$ and the original terms and differentials from $-r$ upward, are bounded-below complexes, form an increasing sequence of subcomplexes, and have termwise colimit $E^\bullet$. By the complex-colimit/homotopy-colimit theorem there is a telescope triangle
$$\bigoplus_r E_{\geq-r}\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\bigoplus_r E_{\geq-r}\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow\left(\bigoplus_r E_{\geq-r}\right)[1].$$
Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,C)$ and using $\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_rE_{\geq-r}[n],C)=\prod_r\operatorname{Hom}(E_{\geq-r}[n],C)=0$ shows $\operatorname{Hom}(C,C)=0$. Hence $C=0$ and $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. This supplies exactly the needed test for representing objects, without asserting unbounded compact-support composition, a bounded-below exceptional-adjoint theorem, or a convergence claim for smart truncations. The exactness of Hom used here follows from the triangulated axioms [def-weil-triangulated-category]: for a triangle $A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}D\to A[1]$ and $h:T\to B$ with $vh=0$, apply TR3 from $T\to0\to T[1]\xrightarrow{1}T[1]$ to the rotated triangle $B\to D\to A[1]\xrightarrow{-u[1]}B[1]$; the resulting $c:T[1]\to A[1]$ satisfies $h=-u c[-1]$. For contravariant Hom, if $h:B\to T$ satisfies $hu=0$, apply TR3 from the original triangle to the distinguished triangle $0\to T\xrightarrow{1}T\to0$, with first two components $0$ and $h$. Its third component $c:D\to T$ satisfies $cv=h$. Rotating the triangles gives the factorization at every position in both Hom sequences. Thus these Hom tests are elementary consequences of the cited axioms.

source.place: Tags 093W (lemma-compute-colimit), 0949 (lemma-colim-hocolim): telescope of the brutal lower tails; elementary Hom test after applying the cited theorem.

proof.text: Use the finite affine chart factorization and gluing lemma [lem-sf-affine-chart-factorization-gluing]. It supplies finitely many affine V in Y and U in f^{-1}(V), each U -> V as a closed immersion into an affine space followed by its projection, with all schemes satisfying the hypotheses of steps 2--4. For each chart, the locality comparison of step 5 identifies f^times K with the composite i^times p^times on K|V, and steps 2--4 give bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude there. The lemma then glues these local bounds and constructibility data to X, yielding preservation by f^times.

source.place: Opening and final paragraphs: affine closed/projection factorization and finite-cover gluing.

proof.text: The coefficient and site identifications are supplied by the two transport lemmas [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] and [lem-sf-etale-proetale-exceptional-transport]. The first identifies the internal coefficient categories, tensor tests, localizing closures, and the module-object compact-support composite with the ordinary A-sheaf categories. The second transports the bounded constructible finite-Tor étale complex K_et and its ordinary right adjoint f^times K_et to the pro-etale object H_K, using the same compactification and the direct-image and extension-by-zero comparison. Step 7 gives the étale preservation hypothesis required there, while [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] supplies the Tor-interval comparison. Thus H_K lies in Dctf(X,A) and represents the pro-etale exceptional adjoint on bounded-below étale-origin objects.

source.place: Closed-adjoint uniqueness and final restriction paragraphs: bounded finite-ring comparison and compact supports.

proof.text: It remains to identify $H_K$ with the given right adjoint on the localizing categories; an adjunction only on the small subcategories would not by itself suffice. Use the right adjoint and natural adjunction bijections supplied as data in the statement. The ordinary étale counit and the compact-support comparison of step 8 give $t_K:Rf_!H_K\to K$. Transpose $t_K$ under the adjunction in the statement to obtain $\alpha_K:H_K\to f^!K$. For every $M\in\Dctf(X,A)$ choose its bounded étale origin $M_{\mathrm{et}}$ as in step 8. The map $\operatorname{Hom}(M,\alpha_K)$, followed by the given adjunction, sends $h:M\to H_K$ to $t_K\circ Rf_!h$. Under the fully faithful bounded comparisons this is exactly the ordinary étale adjunction map $h_{\mathrm{et}}\mapsto\epsilon_{K_{\mathrm{et}}}\circ Rf_{!,\mathrm{et}}h_{\mathrm{et}}$, which is bijective. This holds for every shift $M[n]$ as well. Let $C$ be a cone of $\alpha_K$ in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$. The Hom long exact sequences give $\operatorname{Hom}(M[n],C)=0$ for all generators and all integers $n$. The objects $T$ satisfying $\operatorname{Hom}(T[n],C)=0$ for all $n$ form a full triangulated subcategory closed under arbitrary sums (Hom from a sum to $C$ is the product of the Hom groups). It therefore contains the localizing closure of the generators, in particular $C$. Thus $\operatorname{id}_C=0$, $C=0$, and $\alpha_K$ is an isomorphism. This proves $f^!K\in\Dctf(X,A)$ and identifies the functors naturally, without assuming any unbounded étale/pro-étale comparison or compactness of the generators. The Hom exactness and closure under triangles are the same elementary triangle-factorization consequence of TR3 spelled out in step 6.

source.place: Closed-adjoint uniqueness paragraph and final paragraph: explicit representing-object comparison on the localizing category.

proof.text: Both functors of the given adjunction now take the indicated small full subcategories into each other: $Rf_!$ by clause (3) of [det-ctf-finite-proper-localizing] for the chosen compactification, read through the coefficient identification of step 8, and $f^!$ by step 9. For $M\in\Dctf(X,A)$ and $K\in\Dctf(Y,A)$ their small-category Hom sets are exactly their Hom sets in the localizing categories. Restrict the given natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!M,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,f^!K)$; the same units, counits, and triangle identities give the claimed restricted adjunction.

source.place: Final sentence: restriction of the Hom bijections to the full finite-Tor subcategories.

proof.text:
Finally let $f$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. By the smooth tensor theorem, $f^{	imes}K_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq f^*K_{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_A^L L[2d]$ for one fixed étale locally free rank-one $A$-sheaf $L$, naturally for all $K_{\mathrm{et}}$. The finite-coefficient Tate twist $A_X(d)$ is also étale locally free of rank one: take the same $N=\ell^r$ annihilating $A$ in its roots-of-unity construction. On a common refinement of covers trivializing $L$ and $A_X(d)$ choose an isomorphism $L\simeq A_X(d)$. It induces a natural local isomorphism $f^{	imes}(-)\simeq f^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Pull back along $
u_X$ and use step 9, the derived tensor/pullback comparison, and composition of inverse images $
u_X^*f^*=f^*
u_Y^*$. This gives the asserted étale-local isomorphism of functors on $\Dctf(Y,A)$. The choices of trivializations give no canonical global orientation, so this argument does not construct the later canonical global smooth-purity map.

source.place: Affine-space/smooth paragraph and last clause of the statement: local formula, with no chosen global orientation.

proof_origin.place: closed-support, smooth tensor, and affine-chart proof; bounded comparison and localizing-generator argument supplied explicitly; Zheng Propositions 2.29 and 3.16 corroborate the ordinary étale route

Step 2 uses ordinary forward direct-image constructibility over an arbitrary field, the precise finiteness input to the unit support-triangle argument; it is independent of exceptional preservation and no same-unit node supplies it.
